articles.title: British Masters: Marco Penge co-leads alongside Daniel Hillier as marathon Sunday lies ahead
articles.summary: Englishman Marco Penge shared the lead with Daniel Hillier of New Zealand when play was suspended; Both players will need to complete 31 holes on the final day; watch the British Masters live on Sunday from 10am on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Penge was one under after five holes of his third round at The Belfry when play was suspended at 7.56pm due to darkness, following multiple weather delays over the first three days.

The halfway leader sits on 11 under alongside Daniel Hillier, who has also played five holes, with McKibbin - only playing due to the cancellation of LIV Golf's Team Championship - a shot back after two birdies in his opening six holes.

Fabrizio Zanotti and Shaun Norris both sit two back with 12 and 13 holes of their third rounds to complete respectively, with Jacob Skov Olesen jumping within three of the lead after three birdies in his first seven holes.

Just five strokes separate 19 players heading into Sunday, where play will resume at 7am local time. There will be no redraw ahead of the final round, which will also be played in threeballs and under a two-tee start.

Penge will return on Sunday morning facing a 25-foot birdie putt at the sixth, with Hillier around 10 feet closer after both players elected against putting when the play was suspended.

The pair both completed their final four holes of round two early on Saturday morning, with Penge dropping a shot to set the clubhouse target at 10 under and Hillier getting home in level par.

That gave Penge - a three-time DP World Tour winner in 2025 - a one-shot lead after 36 holes, with Hillier a shot back in his pursuit his second British Masters win in four years.

"It was a bit of a pretty typical me to have a roller-coaster round," Penge said after his second round. "Luckily this one [round two] was on the right side of par.

The pair didn't begin their third round until 6.31pm and Penge's one-shot halfway lead was quickly doubled with a 20-foot birdie at the first, only for him to fail to get up and down to save par at the next.

Hillier moved ahead by birdieing the same hole and two-putting to add another at the par-five next, where Penge saved par after finding the water, before the Englishman levelled again with a tap-in of his own at the fourth.

Norris was the remaining member of that group and he picked up a shot after a smart approach to the second and he will return to the rough at the sixth on Sunday morning.

Harry Hall heads into the final day on five under and Matt Wallace is a further shot behind, while compatriot Tyrrell Hatton is one under for the round and three under for the week with six holes to play.

articles.body:
Viktor Hovland will enter Sunday at the Tour Championship with a one-shot advantage.

Hovland sits at 15-under going into the final round of the FedEx Cup Playoffs at East Lake Golf Club.

Hovland is in front of Ryan Gerard by one shot. There are countless other big names beneath the two leaders.

Scottie Scheffler and Ludvig Aberg are among a group of players tied for third place.

Rory McIlroy carded Saturday's lowest round, a seven-under 63, to put himself in a tie for seventh place.

The full Tour Championship leaderboard can be found here on PGATour.com.

Viktor Hovland is one shot ahead of Ryan Gerard on the leaderboard going into Sunday.

Hovland shot a five-under 66 to get him up to 15-under for the tournament.

His putter came on strong on the back nine with four birdies over the final six holes.

Hovland finished off his round with a birdie on the 18th to keep his advantage over Gerard.

Hovland hasn't shot worse than a 66 all week, so it will be difficult for the rest of the field to surpass him if he plays at the same level on Sunday.

Scottie Scheffler Among Four Players Three Shots Back

Scottie Scheffler turned in a four-under 66 to go level with three other golfers at 12-under for the tournament.

The top-ranked player in the FedEx Cup standings rolled in four birdies and recorded a par on the other 14 holes.

It was a more consistent round for Scheffler compared to an up-and-down second round.

Scheffler is more than capable of making up the gap to Hovland, and he'll have the opportunity to put pressure on him from an earlier tee time.

Rory McIlroy put himself in position to contend for the FedEx Cup with a seven-under 63 on Saturday.

McIlroy produced a 68 and 69 in his first two rounds. Those scores weren't good enough to put him near the top of the leaderboard.

The Northern Irishman still has work to do to catch Hovland, but he's more than capable of making an early run up the leaderboard to challenge on the back nine.

After all, McIlroy recorded four birdies in his first seven holes and had a streak of three straight birdies on the back nine on Saturday.

articles.summary: Norway's Viktor Hovland will head into the final round of the Tour Championship in Atlanta on Sunday with a one-stroke lead.

Viktor Hovland will head into the final round of the PGA Tour's $40m Tour Championship in Atlanta on Sunday with a one-stroke lead.

The season-ending event will also crown the FedEx Cup champion, which was won by Hovland in 2023.

The Norwegian, who came into the third round tied for the lead on 10 under with American Ryan Gerard, birdied the 17th and 18th holes to post a five-under-par 65 to improve to 15 under.

Gerard also birdied the final hole to finish one back on 14 under after a round of 66.

Lurking in the chasing pack are the world's top two players, with number one Scottie Scheffler, the 2024 champion, producing a serene bogey-free round of 66 to finish three adrift on 12 under.

Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy - a record three-time FedEx Cup winner in 2016, 2019 and 2022 - catapulted himself into contention with a hugely impressive 63 to sit five shots off the lead.

The 37-year-old found form with his putter as he holed nine birdies, including three in a row on 15, 16 and 17 to post the joint lowest round of the day.

"I just left myself in better spots on the greens," said McIlroy.

"I gave myself easier putts, putts that didn't break two ways. When I got it rolling there on the back nine, every putt was like a cup right or a cup left."

Australia's Adam Scott, 46, who won the Tour Championship 20 years ago is alongside Scheffler after also carding a 66, while Sweden's Ludvig Aberg posted a 65 to also finish on 12 under.

McIlroy is joined on 10 under by Players Championship winner Cameron Young.

England's Justin Rose and Matt Fitzpatrick are probably too far back to challenge or the title at eight under par.

Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood and fellow Englishman Alex Fitzpatrick are a shot further adrift after both signed for 67s.

articles.title: How Juan Soto views Mets' closing stretch and how he's used off injury
articles.summary: Juan Soto pledged that he would be back before the end of the 2026 season. On Sunday, he made an immediate impact by supplying the game-winning hit.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Andy Green joked he was willing to force his own exit to ensure that Juan Soto stayed in the batter's box for the biggest at-bat of Sunday's game.

In the bottom of the fifth inning of a tie game with a runner in scoring position, Soto fouled a 2-2 fastball off his right shin. The superstar outfielder, who was playing his first game since landing on the injured list on July 25 with a left calf strain, jammed the handle of his bat into the grass, crouched near the on-deck circle and shook off the sting.

"I was certainly hoping we weren't taking him out of the game," Green said. "I was gonna give him all the time in the world he needed. I would've gotten ejected just to give him more time. The umpire was saying to speed things up."

On the very next pitch, Soto caught a hanging knuckle-curve from Cristian Javier and deposited it into right field for the go-ahead RBI single in the Mets' 6-2 victory over the Astros in front of 29,183 fans at Citi Field.

The interruption provided a brief scare for Soto, who has twice been on the injured list this season, but he proved his worth once again by flashing his dynamic bat in a key spot in his first game back.

"At the time, everything went through my mind, but definitely I tried to stay positive and tried to think the best possible way to get out of it," Soto said of fouling the pitch off his leg. "Little by little, I just said [screw] it, I'm gonna try to push through it. I'm going to take too long here. I got be out here."

There would be no denying Soto's path back to the big league diamond.

After Soto suffered a Grade 2 left calf strain during a game with the Dodgers on July 24, the Mets superstar outfielder asserted that he would be back before the end of the 2026 season. A little more than one month later on Saturday afternoon, without a rehab assignment, Soto was back in the lineup as the team's designated hitter, batting second.

"He's worked incredibly hard over the last few weeks. He's done a lot of it behind the scenes without people seeing it. He's done it when we're on the road," Mets interim manager Andy Green said. "He's pushed himself in a way that, frankly, you don't see a lot of veterans push themselves when your team is in this type of situation that we're in.

"I think that speaks volumes to his desire to be on the field, his desire to play, loves the game, enjoying his teammates, wants to be part of winning baseball for the rest of the year, so excited about that."

While the Mets' position in the standings — they entered Saturday's action at 60-75 and losers of three straight games — afforded them a chance to be cautious with their $765 million outfielder, Soto pushed to return.

He began running about two weeks ago and participated in live batting practice earlier this week. Soto said that his calf reacted well to the workouts and testing, which allowed him to return five weeks after the injury. Earlier in the season, Soto missed 15 games while tending to a mild right calf strain.

"It's really frustrating to be down and not being able to help your team and try to perform out there, try to have fun with the boys," Soto said. "I think it's really frustrating. That's one of the things that keep me motivated to be out there again. This is the longest I've ever been out, so it's just day in, day out, just focused to try and come back."

How will the Mets use Juan Soto off the injury?

The club will remain cautious with one of the centerpieces of their future, particularly with Soto also suffering a lower-grade calf strain to his other leg in early April and the Mets' playoff hopes all but gone.

"He's ready to play. We'll check him daily. That'll be a part of the process," Green said. "If he needs a day, he will get a day. There will be some days scheduled at the outset."

In 85 games this season, Soto is slashing .283/.406/.535 with 21 home runs, 53 RBI and 47 runs. He earned his first All-Star selection as a member of the Mets and fifth overall.

Soto said he anticipates that he will log more time at designated hitter following his speedy recovery.

Green does not expect Soto's return to disrupt the playing time of Carson Benge or A.J. Ewing. MLB.com's Anthony DiComo reported that Luis Robert Jr. was placed on waivers Sunday, but he could remain on the team if no teams opt to claim him.

The Mets are hoping that adding Soto to the mix can continue their improved play since the trade deadline. The Mets are 14-9 since the team was shook up on Aug. 3.

"We brought in a lot of young talent from the minor leagues and now seeing them playing the way they're playing and seeing how everything is clicking for us, I think it's really cool to see," Soto said. "It means a lot, not only for this year but for the next years coming (up). I'm just really happy about it, the way we are playing and that's another thing too that motivated me a little bit more to come back to try and join this positive wave and try to carry it on."

articles.title: Tour Championship: Viktor Hovland leads heading into final day as Scottie Scheffler and Rory McIlroy keep FedExCup hopes alive
articles.summary: Viktor Hovland is one ahead of Ryan Gerard as he chases a second FedExCup title in four years; Scottie Scheffler is three shots back and Rory McIlroy carded a round-of-the-day 63; watch the final round of the Tour Championship live on Sunday from 5pm on Sky Sports Golf
articles.body:
Hovland produced a birdie-birdie finish to post a five-under 65 at East Lake, lifting the 2023 FedExCup champion to 15 under and with a narrow advantage over playing partner Ryan Gerard.

The halfway co-leaders were chased down by a star-studded chasing pack during a thrilling Saturday at the PGA Tour's season finale, with world no 1 Scottie Scheffler three shots back in third spot and chasing a second FedExCup title.

Scheffler is joined on 12 under by Chris Gotterup, Adam Scott and Ludvig Åberg, who produced a three-birdie finish to his third-round 65, as McIlroy jumped to tied-seventh after setting the early clubhouse target with a round-of-the-day 63.

McIlroy sits five strokes back alongside Cameron Young as he searches for a record-extending fourth FedExCup title, with all 29 players in the field under-par heading into the final round.

How Hovland edged ahead in FedExCup battle

Gotterup quickly made it a three-way tie with a birdie at the third, as Hovland - playing with Gerard - took advantage of the same hole but failed to get up and down from the sand to save par at the next.

Young birdied two of his first six holes to also get to 10 under, while McIlroy charged through the field and made four birdies in a six-hole stretch in his back nine to increase the logjam for the lead.

McIlroy had been eight back earlier in his round but set the clubhouse target, moments before Gotterup briefly claimed the solo lead, before Hovland and Gerard both took advantage of the par-five sixth to edge ahead on 11 under.

Gerard added another birdie from nine feet at the seventh and traded pars with Hovland around the turn, before doubling his advantage over a congested chasing pack by holing from 12 feet at the 12th.

Hovland converted from a similar distance to birdie the next and nailed a 15-footer to match Gerard's par at the 14th, then picked up a shot at the 15th to pull level with his playing partner on 13 under.

Both players saved par at the 16th and Hovland claimed the outright lead with an eight-foot birdie at the 17th, before the pair traded birdies at the par-five last to ensure they would go out in the last group again on Sunday.

"Super pleased," Hovland said. "65 out there, especially with that finish, I'm super happy with that. I'd say the last few weeks I have been putting a lot better, but it's been hard to put together consistently good days in a row. It's been just one of those weeks where I've been able to put it together every single day for three days.

McIlroy fights back to stay in FedExCup mix

The Masters champion was seven off the halfway lead and showed little sign of a title push when he scrambled a par at the first and made a three-putt bogey at the second, only to birdie his next two holes and take advantage of the par-five sixth.

McIlroy added another from 10 feet at the par-four seventh but failed to take advantage of the driveable eighth, then saw a close-range birdie at the 10th cancelled out by a dropped shot at the next.

The world No 2 picked up a shot from eight feet at the 12th and holed three birdie chances of 12 feet on longer in consecutive holes from the 15th, seeing him equal his lowest career round at East Lake.

"I got myself back in the tournament," McIlroy said. "I think the difference today was I just putted a lot better. I think I lost maybe a combined three (shots) on the greens over the first two days and I probably gained over three on the greens today.

"The ball striking has been there. Hit some nice iron shots, drove it well for the most part. I felt like I played okay the last couple days, just wasn't getting as much out of my game as I wanted to. I pieced it together today and obviously with a better score."

articles.title: LPGA Tour: Ruoning Yin grabs FM Championship lead after late chip-in as European title challenge fades in Boston
articles.summary: The LPGA Tour's FM Championship and the Ladies European Tour's KPMG Women's PGA Championship are the last events before Team Europe look to regain the Solheim Cup against Team USA, live from September 11-13 on Sky Sports Golf;
articles.body:
Yin holed her chip from just off the 18th green, having also posted a 20-foot birdie on the par-three 16th, to close a four-under 68 and move to 12 under at TPC Boston.

The five-time LPGA Tour winner holds a slender lead over South Korean duo Sei Young Kim and Hyo Joo Kim, with Somi Lee a further three strokes back alongside American Jenny Bae.

"I think my swing is in a good spot, my putting and every part of my game I think are pretty good," Yin said. "I'm just going to play my game. I'm not going to play safe when it's time to go aggressive."

This week's event is the last LPGA Tour tournament before the Solheim Cup, live on Sky Sports from September 11-13 , with Team USA trio Lauren Coughlin, Allisen Corpuz and Lindy Duncan all heading into the final day on seven under.

Halfway co-leader Miyu Yamashita dropped six strokes back with a 75, having recorded a nine-stroke victory in Canada on Sunday, while Lottie Woad - the highest-ranked Englishwoman in the field - is on five under after a third-round 70.

Top-ranked Nelly Korda tied-49th after her third straight 72, a shot behind Charley Hull, while European captain Anna Nordqvist sits on one over in her final event before LPGA Tour retirement.

Maguire makes move as Alexander stays ahead in Ireland

Casandra Alexander will take a three-shot lead into the final round of the KPMG Women's Irish Open, after Leona Maguire impressed on home soil.

Alexander posted a three-under 69 in another rainy day at The K Club, where play was halted for 45 minutes due to adverse weather, moving the South African to 18 under and a step closer to a wire-to-wire win.

The world No 38 has five runner-up finishes this season but now has eyes on a second Ladies European Tour title, with Sara Kouskova her closest challenger after a bogey-free 67.

"It was a bit of a slow day out there," said Alexander. "It was tough on and off the golf course with the rain. I had a couple lip-outs, but it was still good. I'm still leading the golf tournament heading into Sunday, so no complaints."

Sweden's Kajsa Arwefjall matched the round of the week with a nine-under 63, lifting her to fourth on 13 under ahead of compatriots Corinne Viden and Louise Rydqvist, while Maguire matched Arwefjall's 63 to jump into a share of sixth.

"I knew there was a low one out there," Maguire said. "I didn't really play it that much better today than I did yesterday, I just holed a few more putts and hit it a smidge closer. I still felt like I left a couple out there but it was a nice moving day."

articles.body: President Donald Trump will return to a familiar role next month when the 2026 Presidents Cup tees off. "At the request of the PGA Tour, and its Great new Commissioner, Brian Rolapp, it is my Honor to accept being the Honorary Chairman of the upcoming Presidents Cup, which will take place at the Medinah Country Club in Chicago," Trump wrote on Truth Social in a post later shared by the official White House account on X. Abington High School will induct five honorees into its athletic hall of fame during a ceremony at 1 p.m., Sunday, Nov. 22, at the Abington Middle/High School Auditorium.

Tickets for the ceremony and reception cost $25, according to a community announcement. Tickets can be purchased through the athletic director's office before Nov. 11. The reception is scheduled from 3-6 p.m. at the Abington Ale House and includes hors d'oeuvres, while beverages will be available through a cash bar.

The newest class recognizes two championship football teams, a state champion golfer, a record-setting basketball player and a longtime supporter of Green Wave athletics who helped preserve the history of sports at the school.

Honorees for Abington hall of fame induction

The 2012 Super Bowl champion football team earned its place after completing a 13-0 season. The Green Wave captured playoff and Super Bowl victories and became the school's first undefeated football team in more than six decades.

The 2014 state champion football team also will be inducted. The Green Wave finished its championship run with a 36-6 victory against Northbridge at Gillette Stadium after a season highlighted by contributions throughout the roster.

Etienne Bourgoin, a Class of 2015 graduate, won an individual golf state championship in 2014. The accomplishment remains unique in school history. Bourgoin also helped lead Abington to its first South Shore League title before continuing his career at the collegiate level.

Kelly Snow, a member of the Class of 1993, joins the Hall of Fame after scoring 1,337 career points in girls basketball. Her total stood as Abington High School's scoring record for more than two decades, and she helped lead the program to postseason appearances throughout her varsity career.

Eileen Walls, the official historian of Abington High School sports, was selected for decades of support and involvement with Green Wave athletics. A 1971 alumna, Walls played basketball and field hockey at the school, later worked numerous athletic events and was a guest speaker during a celebration marking the 50th anniversary of Title IX.

The Abington High School Athletic Hall of Fame Nomination Committee selects former teams, athletes, coaches, administrators and community members who have contributed to the success or growth of athletic programs at the school.

articles.title: H-4 EAD: What the latest US move means for Indian spouses of H-1Bs and why there is no need to panic yet
articles.summary: US & Canada News News: The Trump administration’s latest move on H-4 employment authorisation has understandably caused concern among thousands of Indian families in the US..
articles.body: The Trump administration’s latest move on H-4 employment authorisation has understandably caused concern among thousands of Indian families in the US. But there is an important point that needs to be made at the outset: nothing has changed for H-4 EAD holders yet.The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added a proposal to its regulatory agenda titled “Removing H-4 dependent spouses from the classes of noncitizens eligible for employment authorization (EAD).” The proposal would reverse the 2015 rule that made eligible H-4 spouses of H-1B workers who were on track for a green card to apply for employment authorisation.But this is not a proposed rule yet. The item has been classified as a “Long-Term Action” and, significantly, the date for a proposed rule is listed as “To be determined”. There is no draft text available and no deadline has been set as yet for roll out of a draft proposal. In other words, the regulatory agenda entry is an indication of what DHS intends to consider in the future.Before an H-4 EAD could actually be eliminated, DHS would have to publish a proposed rule, invite public comments, consider and respond to those comments, publish a final rule and establish an effective date. That process would take months, at a minimum, and any final rule could also face legal challenges.Jonathan Wasden, immigration attorney, urged H-4 EAD holders not to panic. “Don’t worry about this just yet,” Wasden said, pointing out that there is a long road between the current proposal and an actual change in the law. He also noted that an earlier attempt had failed to make the regulations final because of problems with the economic impact analysis. At worst, he said, a new rule would have prospective impact., meaning those already eligible for EADs would not necessarily be affected.Why the issue matters so much to IndiansThe significance of H-4 EADs cannot be understood without looking at the US employment-based green-card backlog.For thousands of Indian families, the H-1B visa is not simply a temporary stop on the way to permanent residence. Indian nationals in the employment-based immigration categories can face extraordinarily long waits for green cards because of country-specific limits and the size of the backlog.A recent analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) estimated that more than a million Indians, including dependants, were waiting in the first three employment-based green-card categories as of Dec 2025.Many Indian professionals working in the US on H-1B visas pursue permanent residence through the employment-based EB-2 or EB-3 categories. EB-2 covers professionals with advanced degrees, as well as individuals with exceptional ability in the sciences, arts or business. A bachelor's degree followed by five years of progressive experience in the specialty can also qualify as the equivalent of an advanced degree. EB-3 covers professionals, skilled workers and other workers.The backlog has become so severe that an Indian national whose employment-based immigration petition or labour certification application was filed in January 2026 or later could face a potential wait of 179 years for permanent residence in the EB-2 category and 38 years in EB-3, according to the NFAP analysis.For many families caught in that queue, the H-4 EAD has therefore been far more than a work permit. It has allowed spouses, many of them highly educated Indian women, to work, build careers, earn an independent income or become self-employed while their families remain stuck in the green-card system. In fact, an EAD does much more, it enables them to operate a bank account and drive a car.Nearly a lakh Indian spouses are estimated to hold H-4 EADs. If the programme were eventually abolished, these families could face a major disruption to their lives.The H-4 EAD rule itself was introduced in 2015, during the Obama administration, partly to address the difficulties faced by families caught in lengthy employment-based green-card backlogs. Under the rule, certain H-4 spouses could seek employment authorisation when the H-1B spouse was on track for permanent residence or had obtained an extension beyond the normal six-year H-1B limit.This battle has been fought beforeThe latest move also has a history. The first Trump administration announced plans in 2017 to rescind H-4 EAD eligibility. But that administration never got as far as publishing a proposed rule, and the effort was eventually withdrawn.There was also a long-running legal battle over the programme. Save Jobs USA, a group representing US technology workers, challenged the H-4 EAD rule, arguing that DHS had exceeded its authority under the Immigration and Nationality Act by permitting unrestricted employment for spouses on H-4 dependent visas.In July 2024, the Columbia Circuit court upheld the verdict of a lower court, which had held that DHS does have this authority to grant EADs.What happens now?For H-4 EAD holders, the most important fact is simple: their employment authorisation remains in place today. The real moment to watch will be if DHS publishes an actual proposed rule in the Federal Register. That would open the formal public-comment process and provide considerably more detail about what DHS intends to do, whom it proposes to affect and when.Until then, Indian families should stay informed, but there is no reason to treat the regulatory-agenda announcement as an immediate loss of work authorisation.Separately, H-4 EAD holders should also be aware that DHS ended the automatic extension of employment authorisation for renewal applications filed on or after Oct 30, 2025. As this is leading to a gap in work, job losses, financial constraints and emotional distress several EAD workers have litigated in courts.

articles.title: KPMG Women's Irish Open: Leona Maguire finishes fourth on home soil ahead of Solheim Cup as Casandra Alexander claims second LET victory
articles.summary: Casandra Alexander claimed a wire-to-wire victory at the KPMG Irish Open by finishing 20-under par; Leona Maguire secured a fourth-place finish on home soil, five shots off the lead watch full Solheim Cup coverage live on Sky Sports from Thursday September 10
articles.body:
A five-time runner-up this season, the Ladies European Tour's leading player finally broke her duck with a wire-to-wire victory, highlighted by a course-record 63 on day one at The K Club's Palmer South Course.

Alexander birdied three of her first four holes and rarely looked back, finishing 20-under par and three shots clear of runner-up Sara Kouskova of Czechia, with Finland's Noora Komulainen a shot further back.

Leona Maguire finished as the leading Irish player, five shots off the pace in fourth place, on a week where a record number Irish players featured – nine professionals and seven amateurs, comprising the strongest home representation in the tournament's history.

The week was a battle with the weather from the outset, with Saturday's third round halted for 45 minutes by heavy rain sweeping across the Palmer South Course, while the closing par-five was shortened for Sunday's final round.

For a few minutes on the final day, the coronation itself threatened to stall as Alexander dropped shots at each of her opening two holes - her first real hint of vulnerability all week. But any fears of a collapse were quickly extinguished by three consecutive birdies from the fifth, rebuilding her cushion and restoring control as she marched towards a triumph that had felt a long time coming.

"This one is really special," Alexander said. "One, it's a special event, and two, I almost feel like the second one is as important as the first one because it's not a fluke!

"I can't wait to get home and celebrate with friends and family. The Order of Merit is goal No 1, and the best way to win the Order of Merit is to win golf tournaments."

Maguire, meanwhile, had started the final round seven shots adrift but carried the momentum of a 63 of her own - featuring nine birdies and not a single dropped shot, completed before the worst of the rain arrived on Saturday. She got the home crowd going on Sunday with four birdies in five holes either side of the turn, reaching 15 under.

Sadly for the 31-year-old, though, that surge was followed by six straight pars and a dropped shot at the short 17th before she signed off with a birdie at the shortened par-five last.

Her eventual fourth-place finish matches the Cavan golfer's best result in her national open, which she also achieved at Dromoland Castle in 2022.

"It's been a great week," Maguire said. "The crowds have been fantastic, rain, hail or shine. I think it's another very successful Irish Open in the books and the fans really made it this week.

"Nice to get a couple of low ones over the weekend. Friday was the one that got away but overall, 15 under par is a very solid week's effort and nice to be able to give the home fans something to cheer about."

The timing could scarcely be better for Maguire, whose place at next month's Solheim Cup came as one of Anna Nordqvist's captain's picks at a time when she had missed the cut in four of this year's five majors and gone two years without a win. A home top-five, built on a strong weekend, suggests her form is beginning to click at exactly the right time.

The 31-year-old's Solheim Cup record stands at 8-3-1 across three appearances, and she top-scored as an unbeaten rookie in Europe's 2021 victory. That pedigree made her the only experienced name among Nordqvist's four picks, with Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez, France's Nastasia Nadaud and England's Mimi Rhodes all set to make their debuts.

The LPGA Tour and Ladies European Tour both have a week off ahead of the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup, held at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, where Team Europe look to regain the trophy from Team USA.

articles.summary: El noruego aspira a convertirse en campeón del PGA Tour por segunda vez. Por detrás, Scheffler, Aberg o Gotterup
articles.body: Viktor Hovland firmó 65 golpes (195 total) en East Lake para situarse al frente de la clasificación del Tour Championship con un golpe de ventaja sobre Ryan Gerard, un jugador que ha crecido bastante durante las dos últimas temporadas. A tres golpes está el jugador más veterano del torneo, Adam Scott, ganador de este torneo nada menos que hace 20 años. En el mismo grupo que el australiano se encuentran Ludvig Aberg, Scottie Scheffler y Chris Gotterup (ganador de tres torneos este año), tres jugadores en plena forma, por lo que la batalla por convertirse en campeón de la temporada en el PGA Tour es apasionante. A cinco golpes aparece Rory McIlroy, que se ha regalado alguna opción de victoria gracias a una ronda de 63 que le permitió subir 16 puestos. El líder sabe que no las tiene todas consigo, pero que es importante su brecha abierta con el grupo que está en 198 golpes: “Hay muchos jugadores con puntuaciones que están entre el 11 y el 12 bajo par, y hemos visto alguna vuelta de 62 esta semana. Se puede hacer un resultado muy bajo, así que fue bueno ganar algo de ventaja, sobre todo con respecto al grupo de jugadores que están en ese rango. Son capaces de hacer algo extraordinario mañana [por hoy]. Eso me da un poco de margen. Aun así, tendré que hacer una ronda sólida”. En juego hay un premio de 10 millones de dólares para el ganador, el mayor botín que el PGA haya otorgado en un torneo. El título de la FedExCup incluye además una exención de cinco años en el circuito estadounidense. Hovland ganó la FedExCup en 2023 tras arrasar en una postemporada de tres torneos y alzarse con los dos últimos.

articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 40-year-old transporter who had gone missing from Sushant Golf City was found murdered with two bullet injuries on Sunday, with police detaining his driver and an aide in connection with the crime.The victim, identified as Dhirendra Pratap Singh, a resident of the PGI area and originally from Unnao, was found with bullet injuries to his head and chest. Police suspect he was shot inside his Fortuner SUV before his body was dumped in a canal near Dubagga. Police said he was also associated with a political party.Singh's wife, Mamta Singh, had approached police after he went missing, alleging that he had been abducted by his driver, Ravi Pandit, and some associates. Following her complaint, police registered a case and formed six teams to trace Singh and investigate the circumstances surrounding his disappearance.Deputy Commissioner of Police, South Zone, Mohd Mushtaq, said investigators examined CCTV footage and surveillance inputs during the probe."During the investigation, it emerged that Singh was murdered by his driver along with associates. His body has been recovered, and the vehicle in which the crime was committed has also been seized," Mushtaq said.Police recovered the Fortuner suspected to have been used in the murder and detained the driver and his aide for questioning. Inquest and post-mortem proceedings are underway.Investigators suspect a property dispute worth around Rs 8 crore in Unnao may have triggered the murder. Police are examining the nature of the dispute, identifying those involved and probing whether the accused had links with persons opposed to Singh.Given Singh's roots in Unnao, investigators are scrutinising his land dealings and recent interactions to determine whether the dispute directly led to the killing. articles.title: British Masters: England's Joe Dean snatches maiden DP World Tour title with extraordinary comeback win at The Belfry
articles.summary: Joe Dean equalled the course record with a nine-under 63 at The Belfry, seeing him overturn a seven-shot deficit in the final round and win the British Masters; Marco Penge missed out on a home victory after a marathon Sunday
articles.body:
Dean - a former supermarket delivery driver - returned early on Sunday morning to birdie two of the final four holes of a weather-delayed third-round 71 at The Belfry, leaving him tied-25th and still seven strokes behind Daniel Hillier.

The 32-year-old raced up the leaderboard by firing nine birdies - including four in his last six holes - to post a stunning final-round 63, seeing him set the clubhouse target at 14 under with more than half of the field still to finish.

Overnight co-leader Marco Penge was one back with eight holes to play when Dean finished but stuttered over the back nine, while Jacob Skov Olesen and Niklas Norgaard also failed to make late birdie runs to match Dean's score.

Penge's hopes ended when he found trees off the par-five 17th tee and made a bogey, dropping him three behind and allowing Dean - who had finished over 90 minutes earlier - to celebrate the biggest win of his career.

"It's an amazing day," Dean said. "Obviously it's not been the most conventional last couple of days, but to finish it off like that is unbelievable.

"My goal today was to basically try and shoot under par as well as possible. I'll be honest, winning wasn't anywhere in my thoughts, but just trying to get inside the top 15 to just get enough [Race to Dubai] points to keep me safe for next year."

The DP World Tour heads to Switzerland for the Omega European Masters, held at Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club, where South Africa's Thriston Lawrence is defending champion.

articles.title: Ex-Grocery Driver Joe Dean, with Wife as Caddie, Wins British Masters for 1st European Tour Title
articles.summary: An unlikely champion emerged during Sunday's final round of the 2026 British Masters.
articles.body:
An unlikely champion emerged during Sunday's final round of the 2026 British Masters.

Joe Dean, who entered the tournament ranked No. 292 and not that far removed from being a grocery delivery driver, shot a stunning nine-under 63 to beat the rest of the field by three strokes, per the Associated Press .

His wife, Emily, was on the bag as his caddie as he overcame a seven-stroke deficit at the start of the final round.

"I can't thank her enough for what she has to put up with, with me," Dean said. "It was bad enough off the course, with the lows and stuff. Now it's on and off the course. I hope I made her proud."

As the AP noted, he delivered groceries during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and continued doing so for approximately four years in an effort to fund his golf career without a card.

Sunday came Dean's biggest professional triumph, as he shot a nine-under 63 behind birdies on four of his final six holes to end the tournament at 14-under and three strokes ahead of a four-way tie for second place.

Nacho Elvira, Daniel Hillier, Niklas Norgaard and Jakob Skov Olesen all tied for second.

The British Masters is the first tournament in the qualifying process for the 2027 Ryder Cup for Team Europe. While making that roster still feels like a long shot given Dean's overall ranking, it is nearly impossible to make a better first impression than he did Sunday.

The match days for the next Ryder Cup take place from Sept. 17-19, 2027, at Adare Manor in Ireland.

articles.title: British Masters golf: England's Joe Dean storms to title with stunning round at The Belfry
articles.summary: Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean fires a nine-under-par final round to come from seven shots back to win his first DP World Tour title.
articles.body:
14 J Dean (Eng); -11 JS Olesen (Den), N Norgaard (Den), N Elvira (Spa), D Hillier (NZ)

Selected: -10 M Penge (Eng), T McKibbin (NI); -9 F Zanotti (Par); -8 M Wallace (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco)

Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean fired a sensational bogey-free nine-under-par 63 to snatch the British Masters title at The Belfry.

It is a first DP World Tour victory in his 70th event for the 32-year-old Englishman who is ranked 292nd in the world.

He collected the trophy and about £440,000 in prize money, more than he had earned in total from his previous 19 tournaments in the 2026 season.

"All those painful hours and all the work, it's finally led to something," said Dean, who two years ago was delivering groceries to help fund his golf.

"It was a rare day when everything felt right and the putts were dropping and I couldn't do anything wrong."

It caps a busy summer for the Sheffield golfer who won the inaugural Last Chance Qualifier on the Monday of Open Championship week in July to earn the final spot in the field at Royal Birkdale.

He then married Emily, who carried his bag that week and this.

"I can't thank her enough," said Dean on Sky Sports. "I hope I made her proud."

Dean started Sunday's final round seven shots behind leader Dan Hillier and made a move with four birdies in his opening six holes. Five more followed on the back nine, including a 10-footer at the last to set the target at 14 under par.

He then had to wait about 90 minutes to be crowned champion as challengers came and faded.

Dean eventually won by three strokes from four players, including 2023 champion Hillier, at a tournament that was disrupted by stormy conditions in Warwickshire.

More than nine hours of play was lost on Thursday and Friday, leaving organisers scrambling to complete the event before more forecast inclement weather returned.

Marco Penge, who had a breakthrough year in 2025 with three wins, led on 10 under after a sparkling 65 in round two.

He also started the final round on that total after completing a third-round 72 on Sunday morning.

Five birdies and two bogeys in his first nine holes of round four catapulted Penge into a one-stroke lead with nine to play.

However, a third bogey of the round, on the 11th, halted his momentum and five more pars followed to leave him 12 under with two to play.

Penge compounded the error of a wild drive into trees on the par-five 17th by hitting a branch with his second shot and then had to chip out sideways with his third.

That led to a bogey and with his challenge over, he dropped a shot at the last too to finish with a 72 and 10-under total.

A double-bogey six on the sixth hurt Hillier's tilt at winning a second title. And while the New Zealander had two birdies on his back nine, he closed with a one-over 73 to finish on 11 under.

That left him joint second alongside the Danish pair of Niklas Norgaard and Jacob Skov Olesen who both signed for 71s, and Spain's Nacho Elvira who carded a 69.

Paraguay's Fabrizio Zanotti threatened to trouble Dean's lead late on after firing four birdies in five holes during a purple patch on his back nine to get to 12 under, but he had a triple bogey on the last after taking two shots to get out of a fairway bunker and then finding water.

The British Masters was the first event in the race to qualify for the European team to take on the United States at next year's Ryder Cup in Ireland.

articles.title: Women's Irish Open: Leona Maguire falls short as Casandra Alexander wins at K Club
articles.summary: Leona Maguire's fightback at her home event fell short as South Africa's Casandra Alexander won the Irish Open at the K Club.
articles.body:

Leona Maguire's fightback at her home event fell short as Casandra Alexander won the Irish Open at the K Club.

Maguire's stunning round of 63 on Saturday had put her in touch of overnight leader Alexander, but the South African had enough in hand to hold off the chasing pack.

Alexander won by three shots ahead of Sara Kouskova of the Czech Republic, while Maguire ended the tournament tied for fifth, five shots off the winning score of 20 under par.

It is a second European Tour victory for 27-year-old Alexander, who also won the Czech Open in 2025, and she extends her advantage at the top of the Order of Merit.

Alexander said she was "really pumped" to lift the trophy after four second-place finishes this year.

"It's always tough on the final day when you are leading," Alexander told Sky Sports.

"Order of Merit is goal number one and winning golf tournaments is the best way to do it.

"I'm glad I could get it done and I can't wait to get home and celebrate with friends and family."

It was a case of what might of been for Maguire, who started slowly in County Kildare but her magical 63 gave hopes that she may be able to complete an unlikely comeback.

While she fell short of catching Alexander, she ended the tournament with a closing 68 and, by finishing tied for fourth, she equalled the best result for an Irish golfer at her home event.

The 31-year-old will now switch her focus to the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands after being selected as a wildcard pick by European captain Anna Nordqvist.

"It was another successful Irish Open and the fans made it," Maguire told Sky Sports.

"It's nice to get a couple of low rounds and while Friday was the one that got away, overall 15-under is solid and it was nice to give the home fans something to cheer about."

articles.title: Era repartidor, recurrió a un hipnotizador y ha ganado el British Masters con Nacho Elvira segundo
articles.standfirst: El inglés Joe Dean, que no pudo jugar en 2023 por falta de fondos, estrena su palmarés en el DP World Tour
articles.summary: El inglés Joe Dean, que no pudo jugar en 2023 por falta de fondos, estrena su palmarés en el DP World Tour
articles.body: Tras unos primeros días en The Belfry marcados por las inclemencias del tiempo, el domingo tocaba a muchos completar la tercera ronda y pasar a la siguiente. El inglés Joe Dean (32 años) arrancó el día a las siete de la mañana, a ocho golpes del líder, y logró recortar la diferencia a siete golpes de cara a la ronda final del British Masters. Mientras el resto de los jugadores luchaban en un día ventoso para hacer una vuelta final bajo par, Dean logró nueve birdies más para una ronda de 63 golpes, la más baja de la semana, y establecerse como líder en casa club con 14 bajo par. Marco Penge en ese momento era el mejor perseguidor y estaba a dos golpes del líder en el hoyo 12. Pero Penge, pese a su gran potencia, no pudo aprovechar los hoyos 15 y 17, dos pares cinco, y Dean levantó su primer trofeo del DP World Tour con tres golpes de ventaja. El español Nacho Elvira, el neozelandés Daniel Hillier y la pareja danesa Niklas Norgaard y Jacob Skov Olsen terminaron empatados en el segundo puesto, uno por delante de Penge, el norirlandés Tom McKibbin y el alemán Thomas Rosenmueller. Dean formó parte del EuroPro Tour hasta 2022 y no disputó ningún torneo de clasificación en 2023, el mismo año en que obtuvo su tarjeta del DP World Tour a través de la Escuela de Clasificación. Sin embargo, no pudo empezar a jugar hasta el mes de febrero siguiente (2024) debido a la falta de fondos y continuó trabajando como repartidor de supermercado, al tiempo que buscaba la ayuda de un hipnotizador para superar sus problemas con los viajes internacionales. Un segundo puesto en Kenia en su segunda participación en su temporada de debut le valió un cheque de casi 200.000 euros y, gracias a otro segundo puesto en el KLM Open, logró clasificarse para el DP World Tour Championship, el torneo que cierra la temporada. "Todas esas horas dolorosas y todo el trabajo que le dediqué, finalmente han dado sus frutos. Estoy feliz", señaló. Y aunque Dean ya no tenga que preocuparse por llegar a fin de mes repartiendo comestibles, reveló que no ha cambiado. "Todavía veo a los chicos de vez en cuando", dijo. "Sí, lo disfruté la mayor parte del tiempo. Es simplemente una vida completamente diferente. Todavía veo las furgonetas pasar de vez en cuando por la carretera, así que sí, sigo en contacto", agregó.

articles.title: 2026 Tour Championship: Watch Justin Rose's slam dunk ace at No. 9
articles.summary: Justin Rose opted for his 6-iron at the tee box of the par-3 ninth hole at East Lake Golf Club. What came next was nothing short of magic.
articles.body:
If there was any discussion around which final round pairing at the Tour Championship would produce the most highlight-worthy shots on Sunday, Justin Rose and Si Woo Kim put that debate to bed at the turn at East Lake Golf Club.

Weaponizing his 6-iron at the par-3 ninth hole, Rose went from the tee box to the bottom of the cup — good for his fourth career hole-in-one . It was the first ace surrendered at the hole since 2019 when Xander Schauffele carded a third-round hole-in-one at No. 9.

The big shot helped the 46-year-old Rose get to an even 35 on his front nine, erasing damage done by a pair of par-4 bogeys at No. 1 and No. 8.

Kim didn't waste much time submitting his own spectacular shot.

At the par-4 10th hole, the South Korean native's approach shot on the fairway went 120 yards onto the green before rolling into the hole for an eagle.

Kim's hole-out got him to 10 under on the tournament. He gave a stroke back at No. 11, where he bogeyed after missing his par putt attempt left.

The back nine rollercoaster didn't stop there for the world's No. 13-ranked player as Kim birdied at the par-4 12th hole to move inside the top 10 on the leaderboard.

Rose bogeyed the same hole Kim eagled at before going birdie-birdie to tie move to 9 under through the first dozen holes of day's final round.

What's at stake this weekend in Atlanta? It's a good time to ask considering the hundreds of thousands of dollars that could swing at each and every hole.

articles.title: Kevin Kisner Defends PGA Tour's Decision to Ditch East Lake for TOUR Championship in Major Overhaul
articles.summary: The PGA Tour is fundamentally reshaping its season finale. Starting in 2028, it will split its season finale into two distinct events.
articles.body:
The PGA Tour is fundamentally reshaping its season finale. Starting in 2028, it will split its season finale into two distinct events. It will start with a 90-player stroke-play "Championship Series Finale" that sets the final points list. A separate two-week Tour Championship for the top 32, played entirely in match play at two prestigious venues, will follow that. The format will feature a group-stage week, followed by a 16-player, four-round knockout bracket at a second course. While many are excited about match-play and bigger playoff drama, Kevin Kisner highlighted the philanthropic side, too.

Speaking on the Fore Play Podcast, Kisner revealed how rotating venues can benefit sponsors, hosts, and locals alike. In short, the American professional's two cents on the topic is a player-endorsed rationale for why a single, permanent home in the form of East Lake is no longer the only sensible choice for a two-week climax.

"The fans, the infrastructure, all that goes in place to a PGA Tour event is not on the PGA Tour. It's on the host organization that has to run the whole event, and then in the end and the bottom line, that's the charitable aspect of whatever's left over," Kisner said on the Fore Play Podcast .

"I think that's why there was such a big piece of Brian Rolapp's speech talking about the charitable aspect because he's trying to get ahead of hey if we don't have all that with the local host organization running that we're still going to give to charity in these local areas as part of a new initiative and he started with Tim Finchem who diagnosed with Alzheimer's. He and his wife just gave $13 million out of there as a gift to the PGA Tour for this charitable component."

Brian Rolapp explicitly said the new Tour Championship will "showcase some of the most renowned venues in our sport, including places the modern TOUR has never been before." With this comment, he signaled that iconic, historic clubs could enter the rota even if the Tour hasn't played them in recent years. Besides, he also cited a smaller footprint, limited infrastructure needs, and reduced build-out as positives. All these factors lower the operational burden on the host site and sponsors.

As Kisner noted, the burden of running the event and generating enough revenue to give to charities falls on the host organization. But as operational burden reduces, these organizations can save more, which can eventually go to charities. This is also why rotating venues makes sense. Selling suites and funding infrastructure across two weeks could make it difficult for a single host to absorb the P&L risk. Rotating venues doesn't just mean reduced risk but also increased reach to more charities.

The PGA Tour has already started building on this charitable initiative and philanthropic strategy. It has turned its 501(c)(3) arm, PGA TOUR Charities, into a dedicated platform for direct community investment. The aim is to offer everyone a direct way to connect with the PGA Tour's impact on society. The platform will launch national priority campaigns while preserving the long-standing model in which individual tournaments donate net proceeds to local charities.

As Kisner mentioned, former PGA Tour commissioner Tim Finchem and his wife, Holly, have already donated $13 million to accelerate the initiative. The donation is both a capstone to Finchem's tenure with the PGA Tour and seed capital for the reimagined charitable platform launching in 2028.

With Kisner highlighting that side of the change, the new format could give the Tour Championship a broader impact both on and off the course.

articles.title: Timberwolves officially acquire $24M former first-rounder to make room for Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves got a deal done with Jonathan Kuminga. They finally acquired a former first round draft pick to open up enough room financially fo...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have been pretty active throughout the summer, especially after acquiring LaMelo Ball . The organization is finally giving Anthony Edwards a legitimate supporting cast that could very well make a deep run in the postseason.

The Timberwolves were not done adding to the team, as they recently made another significant offseason move by signing Jonathan Kuminga.

" Jonathan Kuminga has agreed to a two-year, $13 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves , plus a player option, agent Aaron Turner tells ESPN. Kuminga will be a starter alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert on the West contender," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

However, the deal cannot go through until Minnesota has enough financial flexibility to sign Kuminga. The Timberwolves recently made a trade with the Utah Jazz that brought them a former first-round pick while sending Josh Green to Utah. The deal was made in an effort to open up enough room for Kuminga to sign.

"The Minnesota Timberwolves have traded Josh Green and cash to the Utah Jazz for Cody Williams and John Konchar , the teams announced Saturday. The Timberwolves are expected to keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch Konchar, sources told ESPN. Saturday is the final day to waive a player and stretch out his guaranteed salary over multiple seasons," Charania wrote.

The trade was quickly made official after it happened, with the Timberwolves officially welcoming Williams to Minnesota.

"Welcome to Minnesota, Cody," Minnesota posted.

Williams will be a great depth piece for the Timberwolves as he continues to develop his game. This was a nice deal for Minnesota, as it will allow the team to sign Kuminga while also adding a young player with plenty of potential to develop.

Williams is currently on a $24 million rookie contract. The Timberwolves' depth is going to be very good this season, and it could give opposing teams fits. Minnesota is clearly going all in on its future, and adding Williams was another strong move for the organization.

articles.title: Packers Roster Cut Tracker 2026
articles.summary: Let’s follow along with all the news leading up to the cut-down deadline on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
Sunday, August 30th is a big day for the NFL this year. In 2026, the league has set the deadline for teams to cut their rosters down from 90 players to 53 for Sunday at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (5:00 Central), an odd time compared to recent deadlines. Recent years have seen the league require cuts come in on the Tuesday following the final week of preseason games, giving front offices a few extra days.

This year, however, the league's decision to hold a game in Australia in week one led it to push the cutdown date a bit earlier. Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst revealed that in a press conference earlier this week, noting that while not a fan of the shift, there's not really anything he or the other 31 GMs around the league can do about it.

That means that the Packers will have a little less than 48 hours from the completion of their final preseason game (around 10 PM Central on Friday night) to the cut-down deadline. Here at Acme Packing Company, we will be following along with all of the Packers' moves to get from 90 to 53, which will include releases, players going on the reserve/PUP list, and more.

The Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list is one mechanism for teams to keep players on their roster in a reserve role if they failed a physical exam before training camp, went on the active/PUP list to start camp, and stayed there all summer long. Players who go on reserve/PUP to start the regular season do not count against the 53-man limit, but they may not be activated until after their team's fourth regular season game, though they can start practicing after two games have passed.

The Packers have four players still on the active/PUP who are eligible for the reserve/PUP to start the season: Luke Musgrave, Matt Orzech, Micah Parsons, and Jordon Riley. Parsons has generally been targeting the Packers' week 6 game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys, for his return. Perhaps surprisingly, he is not seen as one of the favorites to win the NFL's Comeback Player of the Year award; FanDuel sportsbook has his odds at just +3500 , good for 10th in the NFL. That slots in behind teammate Tucker Kraft (7th, +2700), while a host of quarterbacks like Patrick Mahomes, Kyler Murray, and Jayden Daniels lead the way.

Stay tuned here for news on the Packers' roster as it is revealed.

Running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner-exempt list to start the 2026 regular season , which means that he won't be on the 53-man roster to start the year. Green Bay's roster count is currently 58 players, so they have five more cuts or injured reserve placements to go. Only two players can be placed on the injured reserve as designated to return players before the cutdown deadline. If the Packers place more than two players on the injured reserve, it will be of the season-ending variety beyond the two they are allowed to designate.
